trickyParts: The WarmCodegraph signature change couples internal/workspace and internal/shim through cmd/legion's `cfg.WarmCodegraph = workspace.WarmCodegraphIndex`, so the first commit carries the signature plumbing on both sides (the shim's `started` and the three test fakes) beside the workspace change: every commit builds.

drainWarmUp now waits on the shim's Clock; a shim that never started a warm-up registers no wait (warmStarted), so the fake-clock tests of shims without a warm-up see no stray 3 s wait and a real shim creates no needless timer at exit.

In the floored-wait shim test the kill timer (grace, 3 s) and the drain wait (MinWarmUpDrain, 3 s) are the same duration and are told apart by order: terminate registers its After before the child exits, drainWarmUp only after.

In the heartbeat test a tick that read the stalled holder's token just before the successor's write can still Chtimes after it, so the test waits three ticks between writing the successor's token and resetting its mtime; the observable assertions are the plan's.

In a single PID namespace a successor finds the frozen holder's codegraph.lock live and skips (codegraphLockHeldByLiveProcess), where in a pod the six role containers' PID namespaces hide it; the live stall drive therefore freezes the successor the instant its token is in the lease, which is the plan's own step and what the heartbeat guard is about.

The success line is written to the shim's stderr, which the launcher wires to its own (internal/launcher/launcher.go: cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = m.cfg.Stdout, m.cfg.Stderr), so in a pod it is the role container's log; this pod's own log carried no such line because the running image predates the change, and every later shim found the index complete.
deviations: drainTimeout is exported as shim.DrainTimeout rather than derived in config from MinStopGrace − DefaultGrace − MinWarmUpDrain: the plan left the choice to the implementer; exporting keeps the refusal's message literal-free and names each term.
The refusal's message carries the architect's addition, the arithmetic in parentheses: `… to release its lease (5s + 1s + 3s = 9s)`.

Commit 1 (workspace) also carries the shim's WarmCodegraph signature, `started`, and the three test fakes, so that `go build ./...` passes at every commit (the plan's commit split put the signature in commit 2).

The simplify pass applied four findings in a fifth commit (35e2f512): warmLeaseHasToken shared by the heartbeat and the release; the drain log needle derived from MinWarmUpDrain; captureStderr's restore flag; stage 4b fetching the pod log once per poll and keeping it as the evidence (a timed-out wait now leaves the file its fail line names). The checks and the lease-path proofs were re-run at that head.
`go test -race` cannot run in this pod (no cgo: no C compiler); the race-sensitive tests were run at -count=20 -cpu 1,4 instead (40 runs, no failure). CI's test job is the race lane if it runs one.

The LEGION-629 solution note's formula line (`max(stopGrace − Grace − drainTimeout, 0)`) was updated to the floored form beside the Known edge bullet the plan named, so the note does not contradict itself.

Round 1: the plan's 'on another token, or a lease that is gone, the heartbeat goroutine returns' became 'on another token only': an unreadable read is retried at the next tick, since a takeover's remove-and-create is two steps and 9p can fail a read while the lease is still the holder's (the reviewer's Important finding). The plan's test row 'missing file → false' is therefore 'missing file → true'.
discoveredComplexity: `bun test scripts/e2e/lib` has two pre-existing failures in this pod (scripts/e2e/lib/nats-stream.test.ts: `Executable not found in $PATH: "docker"`); they are environmental and untouched by this change.

SIGSTOP to the codegraph children alone (not the shim, a session leader under setsid) ended the shim with SIGHUP in this gVisor pod — the orphaned-process-group rule — so the unreadable-lease drive keeps the build running on a four-copy workspace instead of freezing it.
